sections.title: The Lead
sections.brief: Open on the state of the league this week, through the people in it. Who tore it up and who fell apart -- named, with what they actually did. Fold in the week's business: any waiver pickup that paid off, any trade that mattered, and anyone whose playoff odds moved hard. This is the section that has to make someone want to read the next one. Three or four paragraphs, no lists.

sections.title: The Games
sections.brief: Place EVERY game and write a note for EVERY ONE of them in gameNotes -- two or three sentences per matchup, about THAT matchup. One league-wide paragraph in front of eighteen game pages is a lead, not analysis. Each page already shows its own tale of the tape, its own big performance and its own chat, so do not recite the numbers; say what the game meant, who it hurt, and whether the loser had any business winning it. The deck is ordered so the biggest matchup leads. Open the section with a short scene-setter about how the slate broke, then let the deck carry it.

sections.title: The Landscape
sections.brief: Where the brackets stand. Who is alive, who is out, who is fighting the cellar, and what next week decides.
